purpose: Magnesium hydroxide is used to relieve occasional constipation and help you have a bowel movement. It is also used to neutralize stomach acid to relieve heartburn, sour stomach, and indigestion. It works for short-term relief and is not meant for long-term daily use without a doctor's guidance.
how_it_works: When used as a laxative, it draws water into your intestines, which softens the stool and helps move things along so you can go to the bathroom more easily. When used as an antacid, it chemically neutralizes the excess acid in your stomach, which helps reduce that burning or uncomfortable feeling. Think of it like a sponge that pulls in water to get things moving, or a buffer that calms down stomach acid.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects include diarrhea, stomach cramping, and an upset stomach. You may also notice your stools becoming looser or more frequent than usual. These effects are usually mild and go away on their own.
warnings: Do not use this medication for more than 7 days in a row for constipation without talking to your doctor. If you have kidney disease, be very careful because magnesium can build up in your body and become harmful. Avoid taking it at the same time as other medications since it can interfere with how they are absorbed — space them at least 2 hours apart. If you experience severe stomach pain, nausea, vomiting, or no bowel movement after using it, contact your doctor right away.
typical_dosing: For constipation in adults, the typical dose is 30 to 60 mL of liquid (about 2 to 4 tablespoons) taken once daily at bedtime or as directed on the package. For heartburn relief, a smaller dose of about 5 to 15 mL (1 to 3 teaspoons) is taken up to four times a day. Always follow the label instructions and drink a full glass of water with each dose.
